from.quote:
The forward computation turns a nonempty row of finite binary32 scores into
encoded softmax outputs. The row length is a power of two, at most 1024, and
scores have magnitude at most 2^124. Its maximum and sum reductions use the
existing parallel programs. Between them, sequential passes load operands,
execute the modeled exponential or normalization instructions, and store results.
These passes provide a simple reference implementation, not a fast parallel
softmax kernel or a GPU performance claim.

passage.quote:
inductive Run (d : Nat) (input : Fin (Sum.width d) → Word) : List Word → Prop
  | phases {maximum exponentials restored summed final : List Word}
      (maxRun : SoftmaxReductions.MaximumLaunch d (Sum.global d input) maximum)
      (expRun : SoftmaxSweep.Run (exponentialStep d) (Sum.width d) maximum exponentials)
      (restore : SoftmaxMemory.StoreLaunch target (Sum.width d) 0x3f800000 exponentials restored)
      (sumRun : Dense.Launch (Sum.shape d) restored summed)
      (normRun : SoftmaxSweep.Run (normalizationStep d) (Sum.width d) summed final) :
      Run d input final

from.quote:
All phases share one global word arena. For n scores, its first n words initially
hold the scores, followed by n positive-one weights and two zero words. The
maximum reduction temporarily writes its result at index n. Each exponential
step loads a score and this stored maximum, computes the shifted exponential,
and overwrites that score's cell. After the pass, an actual store restores the
positive-one weight at index n. The sum reduction can then use the same arena
as its unit-weight dense specialization, placing its denominator at index 2*n+1.
The normalization pass loads each exponential and this stored denominator,
executes rounded reciprocal and multiplication, and overwrites the exponential
with the output. The passes access one element at a time; the maximum and
denominator remain intact until all their consumers have read them.

passage.quote:
theorem arithmetic (run : Run d input final) :
    ∃ exponential : Fin (Sum.width d) → Word, ∃ denominator,
      (∀i, SoftmaxForward.ExpStages (input i) (maximumWord d input) (exponential i)) ∧
      Sum.Output d exponential denominator ∧
      (∀i, Binary32.Normalize.Stages (exponential i) denominator (final[i.val]!)) ∧
      final.length=2*Sum.width d+2

theorem restore_weight (d : Nat) (input : Fin (Sum.width d) → Word) (maximum : Word)
    (memory : List Word) (len : memory.length=2*Sum.width d+2)
    (tail : ∀ i, Sum.width d ≤ i →
      memory[i]?=((Sum.global d input).set (Sum.width d) maximum)[i]?) :
    memory.set (Sum.width d) 0x3f800000 = Sum.global d (row (Sum.width d) memory)

from.quote:
The composed execution contains actual fetched instructions and exact memory
writeback at each phase. Parallel phases retain their admitted read observations
and separate completed-execution witnesses. Sequential passes read the current
arena directly, so their contract requires no concurrent interference. Resetting
entry registers, allocating shared scratch and waiting for a phase to complete
are explicit operations of the composition model. They do not implement CUDA
allocation, launch, waiting or device visibility. No arithmetic value is supplied
by those operations in place of a load or store.

passage.quote:
theorem run_memory_safe {target program s t} (run : Run target program s t) :
    t.memory.length=s.memory.length ∧ ∀effect, AccessAt program program s t effect →
      effect.address.toNat % 4=0 ∧ effect.address.toNat+4≤4*s.memory.length

passage.quote:
theorem maximum_launch_safe (launch : MaximumLaunch d before after) :
    ∃bound : Sum.Bounds d, ∃shared seeds events final,
      ∃run : Runs (Maximum.config d) (Maximum.program d) (Maximum.initial d before shared seeds) events final,
      after=final.global ∧ (∀t, (final.lanes t).halted=true) ∧
      (∃source co, Maximum.Admitted d (maximumBounds d bound) before shared seeds run source co) ∧
      (∀event∈events, AccessSafe (Maximum.initial d before shared seeds) event)

passage.quote:
theorem sum_launch_safe (launch : SumLaunch d input after) :
    ∃bound : Dense.Bounds (Sum.shape d), ∃seeds events final,
      ∃run : Runs (Dense.config (Sum.shape d) bound) (Sum.program d)
        (Sum.initial d input (List.replicate (Sum.sharedWords d) 0) seeds) events final,
      after=final.global ∧ (∀t, (final.lanes t).halted=true) ∧
      (∃source co, Dense.Admitted (Sum.shape d) bound (Sum.global d input)
        (List.replicate (Sum.sharedWords d) 0) seeds run source co) ∧
      (∀event∈events, AccessSafe (Sum.initial d input (List.replicate (Sum.sharedWords d) 0) seeds) event)

from.quote:
The numerical theorem uses the exact real values of the original stored scores.
It derives the finite attained maximum, exponential range and approximation
errors, and the sum's rounding error. If the sum of exponential error allowances
plus (n-1)/8192 is at most one half, the computed denominator is at least one
half. Rounded reciprocal and product then remain finite. Each output is bounded
against the stable real softmax, retaining exponential, sum, reciprocal and
multiplication errors separately. The error guard is a sufficient accuracy
condition, not a claim that other inputs cannot execute correctly. Existence
must not assume successful intermediate arithmetic or the desired output.

passage.quote:
theorem execution_exists (d : Nat) (bound : Sum.Bounds d)
    (input : Fin (Sum.width d) → Word) (values : Fin (Sum.width d) → ℝ)
    (finite : ∀i, Ptx.Binary32.finiteReal (input i)=some (values i))
    (small : ∀i, |values i|≤(2:ℝ)^(124:ℤ)) : ∃final, Run d input final

passage.quote:
def AccuracyGuard (d : Nat) (values : Fin (Sum.width d) → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀m, (∀i, values i≤m) → (∃i, values i=m) → SoftmaxForward.totalBudget d values m≤1/2

passage.quote:
def Accurate (d : Nat) (input : Fin (Sum.width d) → Word)
    (values : Fin (Sum.width d) → ℝ) (final : List Word) : Prop :=
  final.length=2*Sum.width d+2 ∧
  ∃ (m : ℝ) (u : Fin (Sum.width d) → ℝ)
      (exponential : Fin (Sum.width d) → Word) (denominator : Word),
    finiteReal (Scalar.SoftmaxPipeline.maximumWord d input)=some m ∧
    (∀i, values i≤m) ∧ (∃i, values i=m) ∧
    (∀i, SoftmaxForward.ExpStages (input i) (Scalar.SoftmaxPipeline.maximumWord d input) (exponential i)) ∧
    Sum.Output d exponential denominator ∧
    (∀i, Normalize.Stages (exponential i) denominator (final[i.val]!)) ∧
    (∀i, finiteReal (exponential i)=some (u i)) ∧
    finiteReal denominator=some (Sum.rounded d u) ∧ 1/2≤Sum.rounded d u ∧
    (∀i, ∃word, final[i.val]?=some word ∧ finiteReal word=some (resultValue d u i) ∧
      |resultValue d u i-Softmax.rowForward values i|≤coordinateAllowance d values m u i) ∧
    |(∑i,resultValue d u i)-1|≤∑i,coordinateAllowance d values m u i

theorem correct (d : Nat) (bound : d≤10)
    (input : Fin (Sum.width d) → Word) (values : Fin (Sum.width d) → ℝ)
    (finite : ∀i, finiteReal (input i)=some (values i))
    (small : ∀i, |values i|≤(2:ℝ)^(124:ℤ))

theorem rowForward_formula (values : Fin n → ℝ) (m : ℝ)
    (upper : ∀i, values i≤m) (attained : ∃i, values i=m) (i : Fin n) :
    rowForward values i = Ptx.Binary32.SoftmaxForward.exact values m i /
      (∑j,Ptx.Binary32.SoftmaxForward.exact values m j)

passage.quote:
This component selects a maximum from a nonempty power-of-two row of finite
binary32 words. One cooperating thread array, a group whose threads can share
memory and wait at a common barrier, handles the row. The first domain has at
most 1024 entries. The result is an original input word, its real value is at
least every input's value, and some input attains it. Both signs of zero and
subnormal values are included; NaNs and infinities are outside the real theorem.

passage.quote:
The numerical proof derives finite intermediate sums from the input magnitude
and tree depth. It bounds the error against the exact sum of the actual encoded
input values, keeping it separate from each exponential's error against its
ideal real value. A conservative uniform allowance of 2^-13 per tree addition
covers this bounded domain, giving a sum error at most (n-1)*2^-13. The exact
multiplications by one and final addition of zero introduce no real-value error.
A sharper allowance can replace this bound without changing the arithmetic order.

prevent overflow in the negation, addition and base conversion. The proof derives

supported exponential domain. Finiteness or successful intermediate computations
are conclusions, not extra premises. Both signs of zero and gradual underflow
remain covered by the existing arithmetic contracts.
